Dun is the largest single thing in it, at about a third of alleles, and d1 is carried on purpose - primitive marking without body dilution is exactly what a landrace this old should be throwing.
Silver is forced wild. The draft flagged its own 2% silver for removal for want of any documented Mongolian frequency, and that was the right call.
Champagne, pearl, mushroom, frame, the leopard complex and brindle are forced wild too.
Tolerant both ways and cold near-fixed - this is the only sensible reading of a horse that lives out through the dzud and through a steppe summer. Health 10 is unmanaged survival on grass alone.

The desert, mountain and steppe regional types are real and are not strains here: they differ mainly in size and build, and a strain may override gene pools and nothing else. The size band spans all three.
All disorders clear. No Mongolian carrier prevalence exists for any locus, and PSSM1 in particular is a dominant disease rather than a harmless carrier state - it must not be seeded speculatively.
None of these rates comes from a genomic survey; they are gameplay approximations calibrated to the described phenotype spread.
Winter coat depth, hoof hardness, the Roman nose, dzud survival, digging for forage under snow and airag are none of them modelled.

name: Montenegrin Domestic Hilly Horse
notes: Montenegro's native mountain horse, the Domaci brdski konj, recorded by FAO DAD-IS as Montenegro's own mountain-pony population and also called the Montenegro Mountain Horse in English.

It shares that native name with the Domestic Mountain Pony already in the mod, which is the Bosnian half of the same thing. They are sister national populations of one transboundary Balkan hill horse, whose family also takes in local populations in North Macedonia, Bulgaria and Romania. Both ship, each pinned to its own nation, because that is what the country field is for; nobody has shown the two populations to be phenotypically or genetically separate, and this file should not be read as claiming they are.

Grey is the one real difference in the pools, and it is the traditional colour list doing it: dorata first - the bays and browns - then grey and white, then black, then alata, the chestnuts. Grey runs far heavier here than in its Bosnian sister, where the breeding programme excludes it outright.
Every dilution and every white pattern is forced wild, which makes this a solid-coloured mountain population on extension, agouti and grey alone rather than a general-purpose pony.

The colour evidence is thin - one non-academic breed page and a DAD-IS list - and no Montenegrin STX17 or MC1R survey was located. The grey rate is an approximation and is the least certain number in the file.
The sources give an average, about 13.1 to 13.2 hands, rather than a range. The band is set around that average at the width its Bosnian sister carries.
Health 9 for a pack horse that carries a hundred kilos over limestone on local forage, and cold tolerant lightly for Montenegrin winters, matching the sister breed.
All disorders clear. Borrowing rates from another Balkan breed would be as much an invention as borrowing them from a commercial one.
Trail sense, load capacity, hoof wear on karst, forage thrift and the Balkan colour vocabulary itself are none of them modelled.

name: Morgan
notes: Slightly crested neck, expressive eyes, compact and refined - a versatile foundation American breed.
Cushing's, EMS: age-related, folded into heartiness.
Carries W4, the Camarillo white: the line was founded on Morgan mares bred to one white stallion in the 1920s, and it is the only breed here that throws an all-white foal rather than a grey.

name: Murgese
notes: The horse of the Murge plateau in Apulia, out of Spanish rule in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries with Barb and Iberian blood in it, rebuilt and registered at the Foggia stallion depot in 1926 and kept today by the ANAMF.

The colour rule is the strictest in the mod. The palette is raven black and blue roan and nothing else: black is E_ aa, and the blue roan is that plus Rn. Both base loci are fixed, which no other natural breed here does.
Blue roan is about 2% of the population, so the roan allele sits near 0.01 - a Hardy-Weinberg back-calculation from the phenotype, and a restrained one, since studbook mating is not random.

The old language for the blue roans is 'iron grey' and it is a trap. It is roan, not STX17 grey: a blue roan keeps its dark head and dark lower legs and does not whiten with age, where a grey would end up white and wreck the breed's whole look. Grey is forced wild.
Chestnut, bay, dun, cream, champagne, silver, pearl, mushroom, every pinto and the leopard complex are all forced wild as well. The abundant mane and tail are structural and are not flaxen or silver.
Managed sources only. This is an Italian registry breed kept semi-extensively on the plateau, not a feral population, and it should not turn up as a wild pack.

All disorders clear, and the temptation to seed some was real: the pedigree study reports a mean inbreeding coefficient near 5.22% and an effective population near 47, with a small set of ancestors explaining much of the present diversity. That is a monitoring concern, not evidence for any particular mutation.
Granduca di Martina, Araldo delle Murge and Nerone are the foundation stallions. Founder-line identity is not modelled.
Heat tolerant for Apulia. The endurance work, the hoof quality and the Murgese's characteristic uphill carriage are none of them modelled.

name: Mustang
notes: Wild-type diversity: every colour, compact build, hard feet. Some carry the leopard complex.
HERDA, GBED: both carried at the wild rate (PPIB, GBE1).

name: New Forest Pony
notes: Large head, thick neck, flashy movement. Laminitis / EMS are age-related (folded into heartiness).

name: Paso Fino
notes: Compact rounded build, naturally smooth lateral gait - gait is a roadmap item (DMRT3).
EMS, DSLD: age-related, folded into heartiness.

name: Percheron
notes: Large draft with a straight profile and (for its size) fine legs. Grey or black. PSSM1 carried at the wild rate (GYS1); anhidrosis is not modelled.

name: Posavac
notes: The Hrvatski posavac - the cold-blooded farm horse of the Posavina, the seasonally flooded lowland of the Sava basin in central Croatia. Also the Posavski konj.

The smaller, lighter counterpart to the Croatian Coldblood. The two are related but genetically distinct populations (Galov et al. found no recent bottleneck in the Posavina sample), and here the difference is the size band and a higher speed, jump and health, not the coat.
Broad feet and a deep short-legged frame for soft ground. Bred on wet pasture at low input, which is what health 10 is: it recovers on coarse forage that would not keep a riding horse.

Two intake drafts described this breed with opposite coat identities - one bay and seal-brown led with flaxen absent, one chestnut-led with flaxen a defining trait - and neither cited a coat survey. The better-sourced draft (Ivankovic et al., which is also the source of the heights) leads with bay and seal brown, so that is what shipped, with chestnut kept a real minority at about one founder in nine and a mild flaxen allowed on it. No Croatian coat survey exists; this is a gameplay approximation and nothing more.
Seal brown is carried by the shade locus rather than a separate agouti allele, so the shade pool is skewed dark instead of using the house-standard spread.
Grey is a minority. Cream, pearl, champagne, silver, dun, roan, mushroom and rabicano are forced wild: nothing found supports them in a conservative founder pool.
Solid-bodied. No tobiano, frame, splash, dominant white or leopard. Sabino 1 sits near absent, for ordinary face and leg white only.
Free-ranging herds are real here - the breed is used as a conservation grazer on protected Sava floodplain landscapes - so unlike the Croatian Coldblood it keeps its wild spawn.
Cold tolerant for wet continental winters and lightly heat tolerant for the summers.
All disorders clear. A WFFS study finding zero carriers in the Polish Heavy Draft is a different breed and licenses nothing, and 'draught type' is not evidence of a Posavac PSSM1 rate.
One draft gave 'Turopolje horse' as a local synonym. That is conventionally a separate Croatian breed and was not followed.
Traction, harness work, forestry, meat and milk production, fetlock feathering and floodplain footing are none of them modelled.

name: Przewalski's Horse
notes: The only never-domesticated true wild horse: stocky dun body, erect black mane, no forelock, no spotting. Mane shape is a roadmap render item.
OCD: age-related, folded into heartiness.

name: Puerto Rican Paso Fino
notes: Tiger eye (SLC24A5) - amber or yellow iris, no coat change. The breed's signature.
Naturally smooth gait - roadmap item (DMRT3). EMS, DSLD: age-related.

name: Quarter Horse
notes: Massively muscled hindquarters and broad chest - the sprinter. nd1/nd2 give the odd dorsal stripe with no dilution.
HYPP, PSSM1 and HERDA all have loci now - see SCN4A, GYS1 and PPIB. Both dominants, so a wild-caught Quarter Horse really can be an affected one.

name: Shetland Pony
notes: Very small, thick coat, short legs, heavy head - pound for pound the strongest breed. Some carry the leopard complex.
Hyperlipidemia, EMS: age-related, folded into heartiness.

name: Shire
notes: The tallest breed - the scale band tops out around the natural draught ceiling. Heavy feathering (roadmap), Roman nose (not modelled).
PSSM carried at the wild rate (GYS1); CPL is not modelled.

name: Standardbred
notes: Long powerful body, thick neck, sturdy legs - the harness racer (trot/pace). Gait is a roadmap item (DMRT3).
EIPH, DSLD: age-related / exertional, folded into heartiness.

name: Suffolk Punch
notes: Always chestnut ('Suffolk sorrel'), wide barrel-bodied, no feathering. Fixed e/e, no white or dilution genes.
Anhidrosis, obesity: age-related, folded into heartiness. Rare - one of the most endangered breeds.

name: Tennessee Walking Horse
notes: Long sloping shoulder, long neck, powerful rear drive - the running walk is a roadmap item (DMRT3). Lordosis is age-related.

name: Thoroughbred
notes: Lean, sleek, flat profile, refined legs - the fastest breed in the game, and among the most fragile. EIPH ('bleeder') is exertional.

name: Trakehner
notes: The lightest, most refined warmblood - an elegant head and an athletic build. OCD, bone spavin: age-related.

name: Welsh Pony
notes: Small with large ears, a crested neck and a floating trot. Laminitis / EMS are age-related (folded into heartiness).
